evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: At the current tip, `manager_restarted` only requires positive, changed manager PIDs and nonempty, changed invocation IDs. It does not bind the manager before/after observations to the same guest boot. A guest reboot changes both the systemd manager PID and invocation ID, so it can satisfy `manager_restarted` without proving a manager-only restart; the separate `boot_id_changed` check only validates the explicit reboot snapshot and does not prevent that false positive. Requiring nonempty, equal boot IDs on both sides of the manager restart is a routine correctness repair for the existing check, not a new scope or approval requirement.
